overview: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn appeared on the Medford Bytes podcast to discuss highlights from her State of the City address, detailing municipal infrastructure projects, school funding strategies, economic development, and city operations.

items.title: Introduction and Local Restaurant Favorites
items.summary: Hosts Danielle Balocca and Chelli Keshavan welcomed Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn, who shared details about her favorite local dining spots in Medford.

items.title: State of the City Address Reflection
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn reviewed key themes from her State of the City speech, highlighting department achievements, Bluebikes expansion, street paving efforts, and administrative accountability.

items.title: Fire Stations and Park Renovations
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn outlined ongoing fire station repairs and upcoming park groundbreakings, including planned improvements at Morrison Park, Gillis Park, Carr Park, and McGlynn Playground.

items.title: Medford High School Project and Budget Strategy
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn explained plans to reapply for MSBA funding for a new high school, pursue a voter debt exclusion, and manage long-term fiscal planning as ARPA revenue replacement funds phase out.

items.title: Economic Development and New Growth
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn detailed upcoming commercial and housing developments aimed at expanding the tax base, including projects near Wellington Station, Mystic Avenue, and Medford Square.

items.title: Labor Contracts and Staffing Shortages
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn discussed municipal union negotiations and regional hiring challenges for specialized positions such as assessors and city solicitors.

items.title: Tufts University Partnership
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn detailed the city's relationship with Tufts University, noting annual PILOT payments, emergency assistance during COVID-19, and community coordination.

items.title: Administrative Accountability and Closing Updates
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn addressed personnel management and accountability standards while highlighting women in local leadership and upcoming public art initiatives.
